Book of Exodus.fact: The Book of Exodus (from Ancient Greek: Ἔξοδος, romanized: Éxodos; Biblical Hebrew: שְׁמוֹת Šəmōṯ, 'Names'; Latin: Liber Exodus) is the second book of the Bible.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: The book is the first part of the narrative of the Exodus, the origin myth of the _____, in which they leave slavery in biblical Egypt through the strength of God, who chose them as his people
Book of Exodus.fact: The book is the first part of the narrative of the Exodus, the origin myth of the Israelites, in which they leave slavery in biblical Egypt through the strength of God, who chose them as his people. The Israelites then journey with the prophet Moses to Mount Sinai, where God gives them the Law of Moses and enters into a covenant with them and their descendants.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: The Israelites then journey with the prophet Moses to _____, where God gives them the Law of Moses and enters into a covenant with them and their descendants
Book of Exodus.fact: The Israelites then journey with the prophet Moses to Mount Sinai, where God gives them the Law of Moses and enters into a covenant with them and their descendants.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: It describes the main event of the book, the departure of the _____ from slavery in Egypt
Book of Exodus.fact: The consensus of modern scholars is that the Pentateuch does not give an accurate account of the origins of the Israelites, who appear instead to have formed as an entity in the central highlands of Canaan in the late second millennium BCE (around the time of the Late Bronze Age collapse) from the indigenous Canaanite culture. It describes the main event of the book, the departure of the Israelites from slavery in Egypt.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: They also argue that the exodus narrative perhaps evolved from vague memories of the _____ expulsion, spun to encourage resistance to the 7th century domination of Judah by Egypt
Book of Exodus.fact: They also argue that the exodus narrative perhaps evolved from vague memories of the Hyksos expulsion, spun to encourage resistance to the 7th century domination of Judah by Egypt.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: Movements of small groups of _____-speaking peoples into and out of Egypt during the Eighteenth and Nineteenth Dynasties have been documented
Book of Exodus.fact: Movements of small groups of Ancient Semitic-speaking peoples into and out of Egypt during the Eighteenth and Nineteenth Dynasties have been documented.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: However, there is an increasing trend among scholars to see the biblical exodus traditions as the invention of the exilic and post-exilic _____ community, with little to no historical basis
Book of Exodus.fact: However, there is an increasing trend among scholars to see the biblical exodus traditions as the invention of the exilic and post-exilic Jewish community, with little to no historical basis.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: It is 400 years later and Egypt's new _____, who does not remember Joseph, is fearful that the enslaved and now numerous Israelites could become a fifth column
Book of Exodus.fact: It is 400 years later and Egypt's new Pharaoh, who does not remember Joseph, is fearful that the enslaved and now numerous Israelites could become a fifth column. Pharaoh's daughter finds the child, names him Moses, and brings him up as her own.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: A Levite woman named _____ saves her baby by setting him adrift on the Nile in an ark of bulrushes
Book of Exodus.fact: A Levite woman named Jochebed saves her baby by setting him adrift on the Nile in an ark of bulrushes.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: Later, a grown _____ goes out to see his kinsmen
Book of Exodus.fact: Pharaoh's daughter finds the child, names him Moses, and brings him up as her own. Later, a grown Moses goes out to see his kinsmen.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: He witnesses the abuse of a _____ slave by an Egyptian overseer
Book of Exodus.fact: He witnesses the abuse of a Hebrew slave by an Egyptian overseer.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: Angered, Moses kills him and flees into _____ to escape punishment
Book of Exodus.fact: Angered, Moses kills him and flees into Midian to escape punishment. There, he marries Zipporah, daughter of Jethro, a Midianite priest; meanwhile the Pharaoh dies, and another takes his place.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: There, he marries _____, daughter of Jethro, a Midianite priest; meanwhile the Pharaoh dies, and another takes his place
Book of Exodus.fact: There, he marries Zipporah, daughter of Jethro, a Midianite priest; meanwhile the Pharaoh dies, and another takes his place.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: While tending _____'s flock, Moses encounters God in a burning bush
Book of Exodus.fact: There, he marries Zipporah, daughter of Jethro, a Midianite priest; meanwhile the Pharaoh dies, and another takes his place. While tending Jethro's flock, Moses encounters God in a burning bush.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: This is the book's explanation for the origin of the name _____, as God is thereafter known
Book of Exodus.fact: This is the book's explanation for the origin of the name Yahweh, as God is thereafter known.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: God tells Moses to return to Egypt, free the _____ from slavery and lead them into Canaan, the land promised to the seed of Abraham in Genesis
Book of Exodus.fact: God tells Moses to return to Egypt, free the Hebrews from slavery and lead them into Canaan, the land promised to the seed of Abraham in Genesis.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: On the journey back to _____, God seeks to kill Moses
Book of Exodus.fact: God tells Moses to return to Egypt, free the Hebrews from slavery and lead them into Canaan, the land promised to the seed of Abraham in Genesis. On the journey back to Egypt, God seeks to kill Moses.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: (See Zipporah at the inn.) Moses reunites with his brother Aaron and, returning to Egypt, convenes the _____ elders, preparing them to go into the wilderness to worship God
Book of Exodus.fact: (See Zipporah at the inn.) Moses reunites with his brother Aaron and, returning to Egypt, convenes the Israelite elders, preparing them to go into the wilderness to worship God. Pharaoh refuses to release the Israelites from their work for the festival, and so God curses the Egyptians with ten terrible plagues, such as a river of blood, an outbreak of frogs, and the thick darkness.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: Moses is commanded by God to fix the spring month of Aviv at the head of the _____ calendar
Book of Exodus.fact: Moses is commanded by God to fix the spring month of Aviv at the head of the Hebrew calendar.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: The 10th plague comes that night, causing the death of all _____ firstborn sons and prompting Pharaoh to expel the Israelites
Book of Exodus.fact: Pharaoh refuses to release the Israelites from their work for the festival, and so God curses the Egyptians with ten terrible plagues, such as a river of blood, an outbreak of frogs, and the thick darkness. The 10th plague comes that night, causing the death of all Egyptian firstborn sons and prompting Pharaoh to expel the Israelites.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: Regretting his decision, _____ commands his chariot army after the Israelites, who appear trapped at the Red Sea
Book of Exodus.fact: The 10th plague comes that night, causing the death of all Egyptian firstborn sons and prompting Pharaoh to expel the Israelites. Regretting his decision, Pharaoh commands his chariot army after the Israelites, who appear trapped at the Red Sea.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: As desert life proves arduous, the _____ complain and long for Egypt, but God miraculously provides manna for them to eat and water to drink
Book of Exodus.fact: The 10th plague comes that night, causing the death of all Egyptian firstborn sons and prompting Pharaoh to expel the Israelites. Regretting his decision, Pharaoh commands his chariot army after the Israelites, who appear trapped at the Red Sea.

Book of Exodus.question: God parts the sea, allowing the _____ to pass through, before drowning Pharaoh's pursuing forces
Book of Exodus.fact: The Israelites are to take a lamb on the 10th day of the month, sacrifice the lamb on the 14th day, daub its blood on their mezuzot (doorposts) and lintels and to observe the Passover meal that night, during the full moon. The 10th plague comes that night, causing the death of all Egyptian firstborn sons and prompting Pharaoh to expel the Israelites.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: The _____ites arrive at the mountain of God, where Moses's father-in-law Jethro visits Moses; at his suggestion, Moses appoints judges over Israel
Book of Exodus.fact: Regretting his decision, Pharaoh commands his chariot army after the Israelites, who appear trapped at the Red Sea. God parts the sea, allowing the Israelites to pass through, before drowning Pharaoh's pursuing forces.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: God tells _____ to ascend the mountain
Book of Exodus.fact: The Israelites arrive at the mountain of God, where Moses's father-in-law Jethro visits Moses; at his suggestion, Moses appoints judges over Israel. God tells Moses to ascend the mountain.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: God pronounces the _____ (the Ethical Decalogue) in the hearing of all Israel
Book of Exodus.fact: God pronounces the Ten Commandments (the Ethical Decalogue) in the hearing of all Israel.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: Moses goes up the mountain into the presence of God, who pronounces the _____ of ritual and civil law and promises Canaan to them if they obey
Book of Exodus.fact: Moses goes up the mountain into the presence of God, who pronounces the Covenant Code of ritual and civil law and promises Canaan to them if they obey.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: God calls _____ up the mountain again, where he remains for forty days and forty nights, after which he returns, bearing the set of stone tablets
Book of Exodus.fact: Moses goes up the mountain into the presence of God, who pronounces the Covenant Code of ritual and civil law and promises Canaan to them if they obey. Moses comes down from the mountain and writes down God's words, and the people agree to keep them.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: God gives _____ the two tablets of stone containing the words of the ten commandments, written with the "finger of God"
Book of Exodus.fact: God calls Moses up the mountain again, where he remains for forty days and forty nights, after which he returns, bearing the set of stone tablets. God gives Moses instructions for the construction of the tabernacle so that God may dwell permanently among his chosen people, along with instructions for the priestly vestments, the altar and its appurtenances, procedures for the ordination of priests, and the daily sacrifice offerings.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: While Moses is with God, _____ casts a golden calf, which the people worship
Book of Exodus.fact: Aaron becomes the first hereditary high priest. While Moses is with God, Aaron casts a golden calf, which the people worship.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: God informs _____ of their apostasy and threatens to kill them all, but relents when Moses pleads for them
Book of Exodus.fact: God gives Moses the two tablets of stone containing the words of the ten commandments, written with the "finger of God". While Moses is with God, Aaron casts a golden calf, which the people worship.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: Moses comes down from the mountain, smashes the stone tablets in anger, and commands the _____ to massacre the unfaithful Israelites
Book of Exodus.fact: God tells Moses to ascend the mountain. God pronounces the Ten Commandments (the Ethical Decalogue) in the hearing of all Israel.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: God commands _____ to construct two new tablets
Book of Exodus.fact: While Moses is with God, Aaron casts a golden calf, which the people worship. God informs Moses of their apostasy and threatens to kill them all, but relents when Moses pleads for them.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: Moses ascends the mountain again, where God dictates the _____ for Moses to write on the tablets
Book of Exodus.fact: Moses ascends the mountain again, where God dictates the Ten Commandments for Moses to write on the tablets.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: Moses assembles the _____ and repeats to them the commandments he has received from God, which are to keep the Sabbath and to construct the Tabernacle
Book of Exodus.fact: Moses assembles the Hebrews and repeats to them the commandments he has received from God, which are to keep the Sabbath and to construct the Tabernacle. From that time God dwells in the Tabernacle and orders the travels of the Hebrews.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: From that time God dwells in the _____ and orders the travels of the Hebrews
Book of Exodus.fact: Moses assembles the Hebrews and repeats to them the commandments he has received from God, which are to keep the Sabbath and to construct the Tabernacle. From that time God dwells in the Tabernacle and orders the travels of the Hebrews.

Book of Exodus.subject: International Relations
Book of Exodus.question: On this plan, the first part tells of God's rescue of his people from Egypt and their journey under his care to Sinai (chapters _____–19) and the second tells of the covenant between them (chapters 20
Book of Exodus.fact: One strong possibility is that it is a diptych (i.e., divided into two parts), with the division between parts 1 and 2 at the crossing of the Red Sea or at the beginning of the theophany (appearance of God) in chapter 19. On this plan, the first part tells of God's rescue of his people from Egypt and their journey under his care to Sinai (chapters 1–19) and the second tells of the covenant between them (chapters 20–40).

Book of Ezra.subject: International Relations
Book of Ezra.question: The two became separated with the first printed rabbinic bibles of the early 16th century, following late medieval _____ tradition
Book of Ezra.fact: The two became separated with the first printed rabbinic bibles of the early 16th century, following late medieval Latin Christian tradition.

Book of Ezra.subject: International Relations
Book of Ezra.question: Composed in Hebrew and _____, its subject is the Return to Zion following the close of the Babylonian captivity
Book of Ezra.fact: Composed in Hebrew and Aramaic, its subject is the Return to Zion following the close of the Babylonian captivity.

Book of Ezra.subject: International Relations
Book of Ezra.question: Together with the Book of _____, it represents the final chapter in the historical narrative of the Hebrew Bible
Book of Ezra.fact: The Book of Ezra (Hebrew: ספר עזרא, romanized: Sêfer ‘Ezrā) is a book of the Hebrew Bible which formerly included the Book of Nehemiah in a single book, commonly distinguished in scholarship as Ezra–Nehemiah. Together with the Book of Nehemiah, it represents the final chapter in the historical narrative of the Hebrew Bible.

Book of Ezra.subject: International Relations
Book of Ezra.question: The book contains several documents presented as historical inclusions, written in _____ while the surrounding text is in Hebrew (1:2–4, 4:8–16, 4:17–22, 5:7–17, 6:3–5, 6:6–12, 7:12–26)
Book of Ezra.fact: The book contains several documents presented as historical inclusions, written in Aramaic while the surrounding text is in Hebrew (1:2–4, 4:8–16, 4:17–22, 5:7–17, 6:3–5, 6:6–12, 7:12–26).

Book of Ezra.subject: International Relations
Book of Ezra.question: Decree of Cyrus, first version: Cyrus, inspired by God, returns the Temple vessels to _____, "prince of Judah", and directs the Israelites to return to Jerusalem with him and rebuild the Temple
Book of Ezra.fact: Decree of Cyrus, first version: Cyrus, inspired by God, returns the Temple vessels to Sheshbazzar, "prince of Judah", and directs the Israelites to return to Jerusalem with him and rebuild the Temple.

Book of Ezra.subject: International Relations
Book of Ezra.question: 42,360 exiles, with men servants, women servants and "singing men and women", return from _____ to Jerusalem and Judah under the leadership of Zerubbabel and Jeshua the High Priest
Book of Ezra.fact: 42,360 exiles, with men servants, women servants and "singing men and women", return from Babylon to Jerusalem and Judah under the leadership of Zerubbabel and Jeshua the High Priest.

Book of Ezra.subject: International Relations
Book of Ezra.question: Jeshua the _____ and Zerubbabel build the altar and celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles
Book of Ezra.fact: 42,360 exiles, with men servants, women servants and "singing men and women", return from Babylon to Jerusalem and Judah under the leadership of Zerubbabel and Jeshua the High Priest. Jeshua the High Priest and Zerubbabel build the altar and celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles.

Book of Ezra.subject: International Relations
Book of Ezra.question: In the second year the foundations of the _____ are laid and the dedication takes place with great rejoicing
Book of Ezra.fact: Decree of Cyrus, first version: Cyrus, inspired by God, returns the Temple vessels to Sheshbazzar, "prince of Judah", and directs the Israelites to return to Jerusalem with him and rebuild the Temple. In the second year the foundations of the Temple are laid and the dedication takes place with great rejoicing.

Book of Ezra.subject: International Relations
Book of Ezra.question: Samaritans offer to help with the rebuilding, but are rebuffed; they then work to frustrate the builders "down to the reign of _____"
Book of Ezra.fact: Samaritans offer to help with the rebuilding, but are rebuffed; they then work to frustrate the builders "down to the reign of Darius". The narrative then returns to the times of Darius I.

Book of Ezra.subject: International Relations

Book of Ezra.fact: Samaritans offer to help with the rebuilding, but are rebuffed; they then work to frustrate the builders "down to the reign of Darius". The narrative then returns to the times of Darius I.

Book of Ezra.subject: International Relations
Book of Ezra.question: "Thus the work on the house of God in _____ came to a standstill until the second year of the reign of Darius king of Persia." 5
Book of Ezra.fact: Complaints against the Jews under King Xerxes and Artaxerxes I. Letter of officials to Artaxerxes, and reply of Artaxerxes: The officials "beyond the river" write to Artaxerxes warning him that Jerusalem is being rebuilt, and the king orders the work to stop. "Thus the work on the house of God in Jerusalem came to a standstill until the second year of the reign of Darius king of Persia." 5.

Book of Ezra.fact: Tattenai, satrap over both Judah and Samaria, writes to Darius warning him that Jerusalem is being rebuilt and advising that the archives be searched to discover the decree of Cyrus.

Book of Ezra.fact: The Temple is finished in the month of Adar in the sixth year of Darius, and the Israelites assemble to celebrate its completion.

Book of Ezra.subject: International Relations

Book of Ezra.fact: Ezra gathers a large body of returnees and much gold and silver and precious vessels for the Temple and camps by a canal outside Babylon.

Book of Ezra.subject: International Relations
Book of Ezra.question: There he discovers he has no _____, and so sends messengers to gather some
Book of Ezra.fact: There he discovers he has no Levites, and so sends messengers to gather some.

Book of Ezra.subject: International Relations
Book of Ezra.question: The exiles then return to _____, where they distribute the gold and silver and offer sacrifices to God
Book of Ezra.fact: Letter of Artaxerxes to Ezra (Artaxerxes' rescript): King Artaxerxes is moved by God to commission Ezra "to inquire about Judah and Jerusalem with regard to the Law of your God" and to "appoint magistrates and judges to administer justice to all the people of Trans-Euphrates—all who know the laws of your God." Artaxerxes gives Ezra much gold and directs all Persian officials to aid him. The exiles then return to Jerusalem, where they distribute the gold and silver and offer sacrifices to God.

Book of Ezra.subject: International Relations

Book of Ezra.fact: The exiles then return to Jerusalem, where they distribute the gold and silver and offer sacrifices to God. Ezra is informed that some of the Jews already in Jerusalem have married non-Jewish women.

Book of Ezra.fact: Ezra is appalled at this proof of sin, and prays to God: "O God of Israel, you are righteous! We are left this day as a remnant. Despite the opposition of some of their number, the Israelites assemble and send away their foreign wives and children.

Book of Ezra.fact: Despite the opposition of some of their number, the Israelites assemble and send away their foreign wives and children.

Book of Ezra.subject: International Relations

Book of Ezra.fact: As a result, the royal court, the priests, the prophets, and the scribes were taken into captivity in the city of Babylon. Book of Jeremiah.subject: International Relations
Book of Jeremiah.question: The superscription at chapter Jeremiah 1:1–3 identifies the book as "the words of Jeremiah son of _____"
Book of Jeremiah.fact: The superscription at chapter Jeremiah 1:1–3 identifies the book as "the words of Jeremiah son of Hilkiah".

Book of Jeremiah.subject: International Relations
Book of Jeremiah.question: Of all the prophets, Jeremiah comes through most clearly as a person, ruminating to his scribe _____ about his role as a servant of God with little good news for his audience
Book of Jeremiah.fact: Of all the prophets, Jeremiah comes through most clearly as a person, ruminating to his scribe Baruch about his role as a servant of God with little good news for his audience. Authentic oracles of Jeremiah are probably to be found in the poetic sections of chapters 1 through 25, but the book as a whole has been heavily edited and added to by the prophet's followers (including, perhaps, his companion, the scribe Baruch) and later generations of Deuteronomists.

Book of Jeremiah.subject: International Relations
Book of Jeremiah.question: It has come down in two distinct though related versions, one in Hebrew, the other known from the _____ translation
Book of Jeremiah.fact: It has come down in two distinct though related versions, one in Hebrew, the other known from the Septuagint Greek translation.

Book of Jeremiah.subject: International Relations
Book of Jeremiah.question: These passages, dealing with _____'s unfaithfulness to God, the call to repentance, and attacks on the religious and political establishment, are mostly undated and have no clear context
Book of Jeremiah.fact: These passages, dealing with Israel's unfaithfulness to God, the call to repentance, and attacks on the religious and political establishment, are mostly undated and have no clear context.

Book of Jeremiah.subject: International Relations
Book of Jeremiah.question: The Greek version is shorter than the _____ by about one eighth and arranges the material differently
Book of Jeremiah.fact: The Greek version is shorter than the Hebrew by about one eighth and arranges the material differently. Most scholars hold that the Hebrew text underlying the Septuagint version is older than the Masoretic text, and that the Masoretic text evolved either from this or from a closely related version.

Book of Jeremiah.subject: International Relations

Book of Jeremiah.fact: The Greek version is shorter than the Hebrew by about one eighth and arranges the material differently. Most scholars hold that the Hebrew text underlying the Septuagint version is older than the Masoretic text, and that the Masoretic text evolved either from this or from a closely related version.

Book of Jeremiah.subject: International Relations

Book of Jeremiah.fact: Equivalents of both versions were found among the Dead Sea Scrolls, so it is clear that the differences mark important stages in the transmission of the text.

Book of Jeremiah.subject: International Relations
Book of Jeremiah.question: The shorter version ultimately became canonical in _____ churches, while the longer was adopted in Judaism and in Western Christian churches
Book of Jeremiah.fact: The shorter version ultimately became canonical in Greek Orthodox churches, while the longer was adopted in Judaism and in Western Christian churches.

Book of Jeremiah.subject: International Relations
Book of Jeremiah.question: From the _____ perspective, the prophetic role implied, more than anything else, concern with law and covenant after the manner of Moses
Book of Jeremiah.fact: It is argued that the Deuteronomists played an important role in the production of the book of Jeremiah; for example, there is clear Deuteronomistic language in chapter 25, in which the prophet looks back over twenty-three years of unheeded prophecy. From the Deuteronomistic perspective, the prophetic role implied, more than anything else, concern with law and covenant after the manner of Moses.

Book of Jeremiah.subject: International Relations

Book of Jeremiah.fact: It is clear from the book's last chapters, however, that he continued to speak in Egypt after the assassination of Gedaliah, the Babylonian-appointed governor of Judah, in 582.

Book of Jeremiah.subject: International Relations
Book of Jeremiah.question: The theme of restoration is strongest in chapter 31:32, which looks to a future in which a _____, made with Israel and Judah, will not be broken
Book of Jeremiah.fact: The theme of restoration is strongest in chapter 31:32, which looks to a future in which a New Covenant, made with Israel and Judah, will not be broken. This is the theme of the "New Covenant" passage at chapter 31:31–34, drawing on Israel's past relationship with God through the covenant at Sinai to foresee a new future in which Israel will be obedient to God.

Book of Jeremiah.subject: International Relations

Book of Jeremiah.fact: Additionally, in several of these "confessions", Jeremiah prays that the Lord will take revenge on the wicked, for example, in Jeremiah 12:3.

Book of Jeremiah.subject: International Relations

Book of Jeremiah.fact: Likewise, Jeremiah's exclamation "For I hear the whispering of many: Terror is all around!" matches Psalm 31:13 exactly.

Book of Jeremiah.fact: However, Jeremiah's laments are made unique by his insistence that Yahweh has called him to deliver his messages.

Book of Jeremiah.fact: Jeremiah 19:1–13: the acquisition of a clay jug and the breaking of the jug in front of the religious leaders of Jerusalem.

Book of Micah.fact: The Book of Micah is the sixth of the twelve minor prophets in the Hebrew Bible.

Book of Micah.fact: The book has three major divisions, chapters 1–2, 3–5 and 6–7, each introduced by the word "Hear", with a pattern of alternating announcements of doom and expressions of hope within each division.

Book of Micah.subject: International Relations

Book of Micah.fact: Micah reproaches unjust leaders, defends the rights of the poor against the rich and powerful; while looking forward to a world at peace centered on Zion under the leadership of a new Davidic monarch.

Book of Micah.fact: On Tiglath-Pileser's death Israel rebelled, resulting in an Assyrian counter-attack and the destruction of the capital, Samaria, in 721 after a three-year siege. Book of Micah.fact: Some fragments containing parts of this book in Greek were found among the Dead Sea Scrolls, that is, Naḥal Ḥever 8Ḥev1 (late 1st century BCE).

Book of Micah.fact: This article generally follows the common numbering in Christian English Bible versions.

Book of Micah.fact: Samaria and Jerusalem are given prominence as the foci of the prophet's attention.

Book of Micah.question: Unlike prophets such as _____ and Hosea, no record of his father's name has been retained
Book of Micah.fact: Unlike prophets such as Isaiah and Hosea, no record of his father's name has been retained.

Book of Micah.fact: Samaria and Jerusalem are given prominence as the foci of the prophet's attention. Book of Micah.fact: Micah describes the destruction of the lesser towns of Judah (referring to the invasion of Judah by Sennacherib, 701 BCE).

Book of Micah.fact: For example, the inhabitants of Beth-le-aphrah ("house of dust") are told to "roll yourselves in the dust" (1:14).

Book of Micah.fact: Misuse of power denounced (2:1–5): Denounces those who appropriate the land and houses of others.

Book of Micah.fact: The context may be simply the amassing wealth for its own sake, or could be connected with the militarisation of the region for the expected Assyrian attack.

Book of Micah.subject: International Relations

Book of Micah.fact: A later promise (2:12–13): These verses assume that judgment has already fallen and Israel is already scattered abroad. Judgment on wicked Zion (3:1–4): Israel's rulers are accused of gaining more wealth at the expense of the poor, by any means.

Book of Micah.fact: Zion's future hope (4:1–5): This is a later passage, almost identical to Isaiah 2:2–4. Deliverance from distress in Babylon (4:9–5:1, 4:9-14 in Hebrew Bible numbering) The similarity with Isaiah 41:15–16 and the references to Babylon suggest a later period for this material, although it is unclear whether a period during or after the siege of 586 is meant.

Book of Micah.subject: International Relations
Book of Micah.question: Further promises to _____ (4:6–7): This is another later passage, promising Zion that she will once more enjoy her former independence and power
Book of Micah.fact: Zion's future hope (4:1–5): This is a later passage, almost identical to Isaiah 2:2–4. Book of Micah.fact: The promised ruler from Bethlehem (5:1 –14): This passage is usually dated to the exile. BRIC was originally a term coined by British economist Jim O'Neill, and later championed by his employer Goldman Sachs in 2001, to designate a group of emerging markets.  The bloc's inaugural summit was held in 2009 and featured the founding countries of Brazil, Russia, India, and China; they adopted the acronym BRIC and formed an informal diplomatic group where their governments could meet annually at formal summits and coordinate multilateral policies.  South Africa joined the organization in September 2010, which was then renamed BRICS, and attended the third summit in 2011 as a full member.  Iran, Egypt, Ethiopia, and the United Arab Emirates attended their first summit as member states in 2024 in Russia

China–Pakistan Economic Corridor.subject: International Relations
China–Pakistan Economic Corridor.question: China–Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC; Chinese: 中巴经济走廊; pinyin: Zhōng bā jīngjì zǒuláng; Urdu: چین پاکستان اقتصادی راہداری) is a _____ Chinese infrastructure network project currently under construct
China–Pakistan Economic Corridor.fact: China–Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC; Chinese: 中巴经济走廊; pinyin: Zhōng bā jīngjì zǒuláng; Urdu: چین پاکستان اقتصادی راہداری) is a 3,000 km Chinese infrastructure network project currently under construction in Pakistan.  This sea-and-land-based corridor aims to secure and shorten the route for China's energy imports from the Middle East, avoiding the existing path through the Straits of Malacca between Malaysia and Indonesia, which could be blockaded in case of war, thereby threatening China's energy-dependent economy.  Developing a deep-water port at Gwadar in the Arabian Sea and establishing a robust road and rail network from this port to the Xinjiang region in western China would serve as a shortcut, enhancing trade between Europe and China.  In Pakistan, the project aims to address electricity shortages, develop infrastructure, and modernize transportation networks, while also transitioning the economy from an agriculture-based structure to an industrial one

China–Pakistan Economic Corridor.subject: International Relations
China–Pakistan Economic Corridor.question: This is estimated to save China $_____ per year
China–Pakistan Economic Corridor.fact: CPEC is seen as the main plank of China's Belt and Road Initiative, and as of early 2024, is the BRI's most developed land corridor.  CPEC's potential impact on Pakistan has been compared to that of the Marshall Plan, undertaken by the United States in post-war Europe.  Following the proposal by Chinese Premier Li Keqiang in 2013, the operationalization of CPEC is expected to reduce the existing 12,000 km journey for oil transportation to China to 2,395 km.  This is estimated to save China $2 billion per year.  China had already acquired control of Gwadar Port on 16 May 2013.  Originally valued at $46 billion, the value of CPEC projects was $62 billion as of 2020.  By 2022, Chinese investment in Pakistan had risen to $65 billion

China–Pakistan Economic Corridor.fact: Originally valued at $46 billion, the value of CPEC projects was $62 billion as of 2020.  By 2022, Chinese investment in Pakistan had risen to $65 billion.  China refers to this project as the revival of the Silk Road.  CPEC envisages rapidly upgrading Pakistan's infrastructure and thereby strengthening its economy by constructing modern transportation networks, numerous energy projects, and special economic zones.  The potential industries being set up in the CPEC special economic zones include food processing, cooking oil, ceramics, gems and jewelry, marble, minerals, agriculture machinery, iron and steel, motorbike assembling, electrical appliances, and automobiles.  The project has come under plentiful criticism by the 2020s due to the myriad challenges and economic costs it encounters and its general underdelivery.  == History == === Background === Plans for a corridor stretching from the Chinese border to Pakistan's deepwater ports on the Arabian Sea date back to the 1950s and motivated the construction of the Karakoram Highway beginning in 1959
